toolsAdded.description: Read the contents of a file. Supports text files and images (jpg, png, gif, webp, bmp). Images are sent as attachments. toolsAdded.name: write
toolsAdded.description: Write content to a file. Creates the file if it doesn't exist, overwrites if it does. Automatically creates parent directories.

toolsAdded.name: edit
toolsAdded.description: Edit a single file using exact text replacement. Every edits[].oldText must match a unique, non-overlapping region of the original file. If two changes affect the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead of emitting overlapping edits. Do not include large unchanged regions just to connect distant changes.

path.description: Path to the file to edit (relative or absolute)

oldText.description: Exact text for one targeted replacement. It must be unique in the original file and must not overlap with any other edits[].oldText in the same call.

newText.description: Replacement text for this targeted edit.

edits.description: One or more targeted replacements. Each edit is matched against the original file, not incrementally. Do not include overlapping or nested edits. If two changes touch the same block or nearby lines, merge them into one edit instead.

toolsAdded.name: bash
toolsAdded.description: Execute a bash command in the current working directory. Returns stdout and stderr. Output is truncated to last 2000 lines or 50KB (whichever is hit first). If truncated, full output is saved to a temp file. Optionally provide a timeout in seconds.

timeout.description: Timeout in seconds (optional, no default timeout)

toolsAdded.name: grep
toolsAdded.description: Search file contents for a pattern. Returns matching lines with file paths and line numbers. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 100 matches or 50KB (whichever is hit first). Long lines are truncated to 500 chars.

path.description: Directory or file to search (default: current directory)

glob.description: Filter files by glob pattern, e.g. '*.ts' or '**/*.spec.ts'

literal.description: Treat pattern as literal string instead of regex (default: false)

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (default: 0)

limit.description: Maximum number of matches to return (default: 100)

toolsAdded.name: find
toolsAdded.description: Search for files by glob pattern. Returns matching file paths relative to the search directory. Respects .gitignore. Output is truncated to 1000 results or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

pattern.description: Glob pattern to match files, e.g. '*.ts', '**/*.json', or 'src/**/*.spec.ts'

path.description: Directory to search in (default: current directory)

toolsAdded.name: ls
toolsAdded.description: List directory contents. Returns entries sorted alphabetically, with '/' suffix for directories. Includes dotfiles. Output is truncated to 500 entries or 50KB (whichever is hit first).

limit.description: Maximum number of entries to return (default: 500)

Implement paginate_records(records, after=None, limit=20). records is an ordered list of dictionaries. Every record must contain a unique nonempty string id; malformed records or duplicate ids raise ValueError. after is None for the first page or a string id already present in records; the cursor record itself is excluded, and an unknown or non-string cursor raises ValueError. limit must be an integer from 1 through 100; booleans are invalid. Return a new dictionary {"items": page, "next_after": cursor}. Items preserve source order and contain the original record values. next_after is the id of the last returned item when more records remain, otherwise None. An empty page after the final cursor has next_after None. Do not mutate records.

- `records` must be an ordered list of dictionaries with unique, nonempty string IDs; invalid records or duplicate IDs raise `ValueError`.
- `after` must be `None` or a string ID present in `records`; exclude the cursor record. Invalid cursors raise `ValueError`.
- `limit` must be an integer from 1–100; booleans are invalid.
- Return `{"items": page, "next_after": cursor}` in source order, preserving original values. Set `next_after` to the last item’s ID only when more records remain; otherwise `None`.
- Do not mutate `records`.
Inspect solver.py and compare its current implementation with the contract. State a concise repair plan; do not edit yet.

def paginate_records(records, after=None, limit=20):
    return {'items': records[:limit], 'next_after': records[limit - 1]['id'] if len(records) > limit else None}

The implementation ignores cursor lookup/exclusion and validation, and its next cursor calculation only works for the first page. I’ll validate records, IDs, cursor, and limit; locate the cursor’s position; slice the following page without mutation; and set `next_after` only when records remain.

 def paginate_records(records, after=None, limit=20):
-    return {'items': records[:limit], 'next_after': records[limit - 1]['id'] if len(records) > limit else None}
+    if not isinstance(limit, int) or isinstance(limit, bool) or not 1 <= limit <= 100:
+        raise ValueError("limit must be an integer from 1 through 100")
+
+    if not isinstance(records, list):
+        raise ValueError("records must be a list")
+
+    seen = set()
+    cursor_index = None
+    for index, record in enumerate(records):
+        if not isinstance(record, dict):
+            raise ValueError("each record must be a dictionary")
+        record_id = record.get('id')
+        if not isinstance(record_id, str) or not record_id:
+            raise ValueError("each record must have a nonempty string id")
+        if record_id in seen:
+            raise ValueError("record ids must be unique")
+        seen.add(record_id)
+        if record_id == after:
+            cursor_index = index
+
+    if after is not None and (not isinstance(after, str) or cursor_index is None):
+        raise ValueError("after must be None or an id present in records")
+
+    start = 0 if after is None else cursor_index + 1
+    items = records[start:start + limit]
+    next_after = items[-1]['id'] if start + len(items) < len(records) else None
+    return {'items': items, 'next_after': next_after}
